    Version 2.x screens: what the feedback on our summary led to

    Four points were raised on the project summary. Each one got a test. This page shows the tests, the results and how far they can be trusted.

    📌 Key points

    • A feature-extraction stage is what the RSNN lacked. With EEGNet's first block in front, the 17-neuron RSNN rises from 0.420 to 0.527 at almost the same size (752 and 842 parameters), and the 64-neuron RSNN reaches 0.534.
    • More neurons on raw EEG do not help. 256 neurons score 0.423 against 0.420 for 17. The group's 2,560-neuron run did not train stably, so it does not answer the question.
    • With enough fine-tuning the front-end RSNN reaches EEGNet. After 1,000 fine-tuning epochs: RSNN 0.697, EEGNet 0.701. After 100 epochs: 0.513 against 0.621. The RSNN was undertrained at 100 epochs.
    • Recurrence still adds nothing, in the trained RSNN and in reservoirs of 500 to 2,000 neurons.
    • These are screening results, not test results. Each value comes from 9 folds and 58 validation trials per subject on session 1. Differences below about 0.04 are inside the run-to-run noise. Session 2 was never used.

    ⚠️ 1. How far these numbers can be trusted

    Read this first. No leakage was found, but the numbers are noisy and optimistic.

    Table 1. Audit of the screens
    CheckResultDetail
    Session 2 (test session) never used✅ PassOnly session 1 is read by any script (independent code review)
    Split integrity✅ PassAll 90 folds: target not among the pretraining subjects, 80 % and 20 % sets disjoint, all fitted statistics from pretraining trials
    Frozen EEGNet stage comes from the same folds✅ Pass0 of the 58 validation trials were in EEGNet's fine-tuning data, in every fold
    State reset between trials✅ PassA trial's output is the same alone, in a batch and after other trials (largest difference 7 × 10-9)
    Label-shuffle test✅ PassTrained on permuted labels, 6 runs: 0.28, 0.33, 0.28, 0.28, 0.22, 0.38 on the 20 % split (chance 0.25, threshold 0.362). 5 of 6 runs are at or below the threshold. One run just above it is expected by chance in 6 runs
    Firing and gradients (one fold, frozen stage + RSNN 64)⚠️ NoteInitial loss 1.373 (expected 1.386). Before training 38% of neurons silent. After fine-tuning none silent, 22% fire in more than half of the steps. Every layer receives a gradient
    Repeatability❌ Fail29 folds were run twice with identical settings: 14 of them changed, by up to 8 of 58 trials. In a second check single subjects differed by up to 5 trials and the 9-fold mean by 0.04. The cause is the graphics processor's convolution routines, which are not exactly repeatable. The code did not change between runs
    Selection on the scoring split❌ LimitThe 20 % split picks the kept epoch and gives the score. This is optimistic, most of all for the frozen stage (picked twice) and for 1,000 epochs (best of 1,000)
    Like-for-like training⚠️ LimitEEGNet trains with batch 16 (15 updates per fine-tuning epoch), the recurrent models with batch 64 (4 updates) and gradient clipping
    ⚠️ LimitOnly a run scored once on session 2 can confirm any of this. That run needs the group's agreement on which version to score.

    🧠 2. "17 neurons are too few"

    On raw EEG, more neurons did not raise accuracy. The largest model failed to train.

    Table 2. RSNN on raw EEG (22 values per step, 256 steps), session-1 screen
    ModelPara-metersBefore fine-tuning (288 trials)After, training splitAfter, 20 % splitGap to RSNN 17Subjects
    RSNN, 17 LIF neurons (group architecture, screen settings)7520.2850.4260.420
    RSNN, 256 LIF neurons724520.2840.5120.423+0.0044 better, 4 worse
    RSNN, 1,024 LIF neurons10762280.2880.4830.400-0.0193 better, 5 worse
    💡 ReadingA training loss above 1.386 means the network is wrong on its own training data. The 2,560-neuron model collapsed in training, so its score of 0.341 on session 2 shows a training failure and not the effect of size. The 256-neuron screen trains without collapse and still gains nothing (0.423 against 0.420).

    ⚠️ CautionThe ELU twin with a trained front end (0.449) has two subjects below chance. Its loss spikes far above the guess level, so this is unstable training and not a property of non-spiking units. With the frozen stage the ELU twin scores 0.649.

    📈 4. Training behaviour: loss against epoch

    The front-end RSNN stops fine-tuning too early. A learning-rate schedule did not help. Longer fine-tuning did.

    Table 5. Effect of the training schedule (20 % split)
    SettingFront end + RSNN 64EEGNet
    100 fine-tuning epochs, fixed learning rate0.5130.621
    300 fine-tuning epochs0.6510.674
    1,000 fine-tuning epochs0.6970.701
    Median kept epoch within 1,000701903
    v2.2c: warm-up and cosine schedule, 100 epochs0.4980.571
    💡 ReadingWith batch 64 the RSNN gets 4 weight updates per fine-tuning epoch and EEGNet 15. At 100 epochs the RSNN is far from finished. At 1,000 epochs both models are close. Longer runs also give the selection more epochs to choose from, so the absolute values are optimistic for both.

    🌊 5. "Try reservoir computing with 500 to 2,000 neurons"

    Larger reservoirs score higher, but recurrence lowers the score at every size.

    Table 6. Reservoir, 20 % split
    NeuronsRaw EEG, no recurrenceRaw EEG, recurrentBand input, no recurrenceBand input, recurrent
    5000.4830.4560.5150.479
    1,0000.4870.4460.5590.502
    2,0000.5110.4920.5650.533
    💡 ReadingA reservoir of 2,000 neurons on fixed mu and beta band inputs reaches 0.565 with only the dense layer trained. That is the level of the trained front-end RSNN at 100 epochs. The recurrent version is lower for 5 or 6 of 9 subjects at every size, so the gain comes from the number of random features and not from recurrence.

    🎛️ 6. "How are the 22 channels presented to the network?"

    Table 7. Input of the recurrent layer
    ItemOriginal RSNNv2.2 (with front end)
    Values per time step22: one EEG sample of every channel, standardized per channel8: outputs of the spatial filters
    Time steps256 (one per sample, 7.8 ms)64 (average of 4 samples, 31 ms)
    How the input entersA dense layer (22 → neurons) gives the input current of each neuron at each step. No spike encoding of the inputThe same with 8 inputs
    Memory of a neuronLeak 0.9 per step: time constant about 74 msLeak 0.9 per step of 31 ms: about 300 ms
    OutputMean spike rate of each neuron over the trial, then a dense layerThe same
    ⚠️ LimitThe output averages the spikes over the whole trial, so the order of events inside a trial is not used. This may be why recurrence adds nothing in any version.

    🔬 7. What EEGNet's front end extracts

    💡 Reading29 % of the filters peak in the mu band (8 to 13 Hz) and 47 % in the beta band (13 to 30 Hz). The 4 to 8 Hz range is suppressed by about 20 dB. The largest spatial weights are at CP3, C3, CP4, Cz and C4, over the sensorimotor area. A one-layer RSNN on raw samples has no such band and spatial filters.

    ❓ 8. Questions for the meeting

    #Question
    1Is a convolutional front end followed by a recurrent spiking layer still an RSNN for our research question, or a hybrid model?
    2Which fairness rule should the final comparison use: the same front end for all models, the same number of neurons, or the same number of parameters?
    3Should the front end be trained with the RSNN, or shared with EEGNet and frozen?
    4Recurrence adds nothing in every version. Is a readout that keeps the time course (for example the last state, or several time windows) the right next step?
    5Which learning rate and initialisation are usual for a recurrent spiking layer with thousands of neurons? Ours collapsed at 2,560.
    6Is pooling to 64 steps acceptable, or should the recurrent layer see all 256 steps?
    7Which one version should get the single scored run on session 2?

    📘 Glossary

    Short formFull form and meaning
    20 % splitThe 58 trials of the target's session 1 that are not used for fine-tuning. They select the kept epoch and give the score
    EEGElectroencephalography
    ELUExponential linear unit, a smooth activation without an upper limit
    FoldOne target subject with one choice of pretraining subjects
    LIFLeaky integrate-and-fire spiking neuron
    RNNRecurrent neural network with non-spiking units. Here the twin of the RSNN
    RSNNRecurrent spiking neural network
    ReservoirA recurrent network with fixed random weights. Only the dense layer after it is trained
    Spectral radiusThe largest absolute eigenvalue of the recurrent weight matrix. It sets how strongly activity feeds back
